evidence.detail: Last comment: 4G setting showed no statistically significant improvement over 512M for the specific slow query (2m13s vs 2m8s)
8G caused MySQL to stop responding; rolled back to 4G; owner states machine has 16G RAM and 4G is current setting
No code in this repo controls innodb_buffer_pool_size — this is a pure server configuration task

triage.notes: This requires server admin access to set innodb_buffer_pool_size in my.cnf (not a runtime SET GLOBAL) so it persists across restarts. The empirical data collected shows 4G vs 512M made no significant difference for the specific long-running cache query, so further investigation of the slow query itself may be warranted rather than tuning the buffer pool.
